minutes.headline: Council on Aging welcomed new director Deborah Goodel and heard the FY26 budget outlook is bleak, with no new hires or hours.
minutes.summary: The Council on Aging introduced its incoming director, approved prior minutes, and heard updates on the town master plan, the closed Nashoba Valley Medical Center, and the FY26 budget, which the interim town manager signaled would not support new hires or added hours. Members also discussed the Passos building and the public access committee's space, capital items at the senior center, and upcoming events. The only formal votes were approving minutes and adjourning.

budget_items.what_was_said: The interim town manager told department heads not to ask for new hires or more hours. Extra department-head meetings are scheduled over the next two weeks, and no reason was given for them.
The director has not received the information from the state Executive Office of Elder Affairs needed for the annual report. She wants it done before she leaves.
The parking lot is in next year's capital plan; no further detail given.
Flooring is expected in a future capital plan and the kitchen is not in this year. Even cabinet work or an addition is not possible given the hiring freeze.
The supporters group has a new board and was nearly lost. It provides a sizeable yearly amount toward programs.
One renovation plan was described as costing a very large amount, while another would demolish the back and refurbish the front.
Two members offered to contribute toward window shades; an in-kind donation was suggested as the easiest route.

decisions.decision: Ideas for the town's 300th anniversary will be put on the agenda for the next meeting.
Gifts such as window shades will likely be handled as in-kind donations, to be worked out with the town.
A liaison to the supporters group will be discussed at the next meeting.
Nashoba Valley Medical Center stays on the agenda so the public can be kept informed.

what_happened.line: The Council on Aging introduced its incoming director, Deborah Goodel, and members introduced themselves.
The interim town manager told department heads not to ask for new hires or more hours in the FY26 budget.
The director said the senior center's flooring is expected in a future capital plan, the kitchen is not in this year, and a hiring freeze rules out cabinet work or an addition.
The parking lot is in next year's capital plan, and the Nashoba Valley Medical Center stays on the agenda so the public can be kept informed.
The only formal votes were approving prior minutes and adjourning; the supporters group liaison was left for the next meeting.

why_it_matters: The senior center's staffing and hours look likely to stay as they are in FY26, so any added service or longer opening time would not come from this budget.
Improvements such as flooring, a kitchen or an addition depend on later capital plans, and any that need town funds could come before voters.
